The ''' 1940 [[German football championship]]''', the 33rd edition of the competition, was won by [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]], the club's fifth German championship, by defeating [[Dresdner SC]] 1–0 in the final. Both clubs would continue to be strong sides during the [[Second World War]] editions of the German championship with Schalke making a losing appearance in the 1941 final before winning again in 1942 while Dresden was crowned German champions in 1943 and 1944.<ref name="List" >[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duitchamp.html (West) Germany -List of champions] rsssf.org, accessed: 27 December 2015</ref><ref>[http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/fc-schalke-04/1/ FC Schalke 04 » Steckbrief] {{in lang|de}} Weltfussball.de – FC Schalke 04 honours, accessed: 27 December 2015</ref><ref>[http://www.weltfussball.de/teams/dresdner-sc/1/ Dresdner SC » Steckbrief] {{in lang|de}} Weltfussball.de – Dresdner SC honours, accessed: 27 December 2015</ref>

Schalke's 16–0 win over [[CSC 03 Kassel]] in the group stages was the highest win in the history of the German championship as well as the most goals scored in a game.<ref>[http://www.weltfussball.de/statistik/deutsche-meisterschaft/3/ Deutsche Meisterschaft » Statistik » Die höchsten Siege] (in German) Weltfussball.de, highest wins, accessed: 1 January 2016</ref>

[[SK Rapid Wien|Rapid Wien]]'s [[Franz Binder]] became the 1940 championships top scorer with 14 goals, a new record that would be broken the following year by Schalke's [[Hermann Eppenhoff]] when he scored 15 goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/deutsche-meisterschaft/ |title=Deutsche Meisterschaft » Torschützenkönige |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 2 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=German championship: Top goal scorer}}</ref>

The eighteen [[1939–40 Gauliga|1939–40]] [[Gauliga]] champions, the same number as in [[1939 German football championship|1939]],<ref name="ReferenceA">''kicker Allmanach 1990'', page: 243-245</ref> competed in a group stage with the four group winners advancing to the semi-finals. The two semi-final winners then contested the 1940 championship final. The groups were divided into three with four clubs and one with six clubs with the latter, in turn, subdivided into two groups of three teams each and a final of these group winners to determine the overall group champions.<ref name="Rsssf" >[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/duithistpre45.html German championship 1940] rsssf.org, accessed: 26 December 2015</ref>

In the following season, the German championship was played with twenty clubs. From there it gradually expanded further through a combination of territorial expansion of [[Nazi Germany]] and the sub-dividing of the Gauligas in later years, reaching a strength of thirty-one in its last completed season, 1943–44.<ref name="ReferenceA"/>
